title: Saying who does not have something
summary: Put the possessor first, fixed ei ole next, and the singular partitive noun last.
prerequisiteSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession
objectives: Say who does not have something using ei ole and the negative noun form.
Recognise the pattern, then produce it with the supporting words shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Put the possessor first, fixed ei ole next, and the singular partitive noun last.
keyPoints: owner + ei ole + singular partitive noun

sections.title: Regular noun forms in these examples
paragraphs: These forms name the thing after ei ole. The prompts show the noun form whenever forming it is outside this lesson’s target.
keyPoints: kissa (“cat”) → kissaa (“a cat”): regular singular partitive
koira (“dog”) → koiraa (“a dog”): regular singular partitive
tyyny (“pillow”) → tyynyä (“a pillow”): regular singular partitive
peli (“game”) → peliä (“a game”): regular singular partitive

examples.english: I do not have a car.
steps: Begin with the owner minulla. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive autoa (“a car”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: You do not have a ball.
steps: Begin with the owner sinulla. sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive palloa (“a ball”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: She does not have a pen.
steps: Begin with the owner hänellä. hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive kynää (“a pen”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: We do not have a dog.
steps: Begin with the owner meillä. meillä means “we as the owner”.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive koiraa (“a dog”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: You do not have a book.
steps: Begin with the owner teillä. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive kirjaa (“a book”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: They do not have a cat.
steps: Begin with the owner heillä. heillä means “they as the owner”.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive kissaa (“a cat”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: I do not have a game.
steps: Begin with the owner minulla. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive peliä (“a game”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: You do not have a pillow.
steps: Begin with the owner teillä. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive tyynyä (“a pillow”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

commonMistakes: Keep the requested order: owner + ei ole + partitive noun. Do not leave out ole.
Retain the noun ending when assembling the full sentence: Minulla ei ole koiraa, rather than Minulla ei ole koira.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: he has the learned possession form heillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Possession uses fixed ei with every owner; do not change it to en, emme, or eivät.
After ei, olla uses ole. Together ei ole means “do not have” or “does not have” here.
pallo + -a = palloa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.
